correctness.rationale: Verified exact scale-two ball/closed-neighborhood equivalence from Adams et al. Every two distinct neighborhood generators intersect in at most two vertices by the local hypotheses; descending-size free-face removals are individually valid, and the remaining unique length-two chords collapse onto the graph plus one full tetrahedral boundary for each four-cycle. A choice of one disk per square forms Q(G), and each remaining disk has nullhomotopic attaching map, proving the CW wedge splitting for all finite admissible graphs. The torus-grid hypotheses and square count are valid for both cycle lengths at least five; the cup pairing follows from the torus summand. Actual exact checker performs each elementary collapse and verifies complete residual equality for 429 labeled small test graphs and seven larger examples, with independent mod-two homology; finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Adams–Shukla–Singh prove the required neighborhood description and a special hypercube wedge theorem; no general square-completion decomposition or genus-carrying toroidal-grid result follows. Previte (2014) studies the identical D-neighborhood object, including the C4 and cube examples and one-point-union homology; these results do not give the universal square-CW homotopy splitting for overlapping 4-cycles. Matsushita studies the same closed-neighborhood complex but its relevant general results are suspension/independence relations and path-homotopy fundamental groups, which do not fix the full 2-dimensional homotopy type. Shukla treats open-neighborhood complexes. Mathematical alias, implication, and available published-record searches found no covering equivalent; risk of unindexed overlap persists.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies scale-two intrinsic Čech homotopy for an infinite natural graph class of unbounded maximum degree, many intersecting 4-cycles, and nontrivial higher-genus square completions. Its toroidal grid corollary gives a nonzero integral degree-one cup product alongside an exact mn-sphere count, a phenomenon not expressible as a wedge of spheres. The explicit collapse model and direct CW topology are mathematically reusable and substantially more informative than a finite Betti-number recalculation.
